correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=3 and every P,Q,B>0, the proof computes two independent Laplacian projector trace bounds that apply to all individually chosen nonnegative edge conductances. Their exact price-dependent linear combination gives the global bound; the direct two-class spectrum attains it. Equality in the positive projectors forces E_- to be a Fiedler eigenspace and hence all off-diagonal entries and all diagonal entries in the bipartite conductance matrix to be constant, and E_+ or the strict cost inequality forces the appropriate regime. At the critical price ratio the full remaining one-dimensional segment and no other allocations satisfy equality. The independently executed verifier passed 4506 exact symbolic/rational and numerical checks, supplementary to the universal proof.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies a natural exact two-price network investment problem over infinitely many balanced complete bipartite sizes, not a hand-picked finite computation: a sharp matching-deletion threshold, surprising equal-edge optimality below threshold despite asymmetric prices, strict-phase uniqueness among all individual edge allocations, and a true continuum precisely at criticality. This provides exact benchmarks for continuous-time fastest-mixing design, where general SDPs need not expose the full optimizer set.
